# Baghdad 830 – Chemistry

- **Soap** [`soap`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/soap.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Soap (sabun) from oil and alkali is made in Syria and sold in Baghdad; many still wash with ushnan ash, clay and potash. Recipes vary by workshop and the strength of the lye is guesswork. Local: soap from Syria (later famous at Aleppo and Nablus); ushnan sellers.
- **Distillation of strong alcohol (aqua vitae)** [`distillation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/distillation.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The alembic (al-anbiq, from Greek ambix) distils rosewater and scents on an industrial scale; al-Kindi will write a book of perfume recipes and distillations. Spirit from wine is at most a curiosity, and wine is forbidden. Local: rosewater distillers (rosewater from Fars and Jur); al-Kindi; perfumers' market.
- **Sulphuric acid (oil of vitriol)** [`sulphuric_acid`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sulphuric_acid.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Green and blue vitriols (zaj) are sold by druggists and dyers. Distilling them gives a sharp water, but no one has isolated the acid; the Jabirian writings that are often cited for this are later and disputed. Local: druggists and dyers (vitriol, alum).
- **Oxygen and combustion** [`oxygen_combustion`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oxygen_combustion.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Fire is an element; things burn because they contain fire. A candle under an inverted jar going out is in Philo's Greek Pneumatics, read as the air being consumed.
- **Nitric acid (aqua fortis)** [`nitric_acid`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nitric_acid.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Needs saltpetre, which is unknown here. Alchemists dissolve metals only with mercury and with sharp salts.
- **Saltpetre from nitre beds** [`saltpetre_production`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/saltpetre_production.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Saltpetre is not known by name; 'snow of China' is a 13th-century term. Efflorescences on old walls and dung heaps are taken for ordinary salts. Chinese alchemists already purify it. Elsewhere: Tang China, alchemists' saltpetre.
- **Chemical elements and conservation of mass** [`chemical_elements`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/chemical_elements.md) — K1, use wrong, make medium, accept low. Four elements and four qualities, after Aristotle and Galen. The Book of the Secret of Creation attributed to Apollonius (Balinus), possibly composed under al-Ma'mun, teaches that metals are made of sulphur and mercury, the basis of later alchemy. Transmutation is believed possible. Local: alchemists and the Sirr al-khaliqa; al-Kindi, a sceptic of transmutation.
- **Atomic theory and fixed proportions** [`atomic_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atomic_theory.md) — K2, use wrong, make medium, accept medium. The theologian Abu al-Hudhayl teaches that bodies are made of indivisible parts that God recreates every instant; his nephew and pupil al-Nazzam denies atoms and says bodies are infinitely divisible. A theological argument, nothing chemical. Local: Abu al-Hudhayl al-Allaf; al-Nazzam.

- **Gas laws (pressure, volume, temperature)** [`gas_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gas_laws.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Philo and Hero describe air expanding in heated vessels in their Greek pneumatics. Without a pump or sealed tube nothing can be measured.
- **Collecting and telling apart gases (hydrogen, fixed air)** [`pneumatic_chemistry_gases`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pneumatic_chemistry_gases.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. All gases are air or smoke. Marsh gas bubbles in the Batiha and fumes at the naphtha springs are noticed, never collected.
- **Acids, alkalis and indicators** [`acids_bases_ph`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/acids_bases_ph.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Vinegar, sour juices, vitriols and alum are sharp; qili and ushnan are their opposite and used to wash and to make glass. No indicator; dyers judge by colour change of their vats. Local: dyers and glassmakers.
- **Hydrochloric acid and aqua regia** [`hydrochloric_acid_aqua_regia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydrochloric_acid_aqua_regia.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Sal ammoniac (nushadir) comes from Central Asian volcanic vents and is prized by alchemists and metalworkers. Isolating an acid from salt and vitriol is not done. Elsewhere: Central Asia (Ustrushana, the Buttam mountains), sal ammoniac.
- **Alkalis (potash, soda, caustic lye)** [`alkali_soda`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alkali_soda.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Plant ash (qili, from saltworts of the desert edge) feeds glassmakers and soap boilers and gives English 'alkali' later. Lye is made by leaching ash, sometimes sharpened with lime. Local: ushnan and qili burners; glass workshops of Raqqa and Iraq.
- **Lime burning and lime mortar** [`lime_burning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lime_burning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Baghdad is built of sun-dried and fired brick laid in gypsum plaster (juss), burnt in kilns along the Tigris; lime is burnt too. Juss is cheap and fast but weak in wet places. Local: juss burners and brickmakers.
- **Salt making (sea salt, brine boiling, rock salt)** [`salt_production`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/salt_production.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Salt comes from salt flats and marshes of lower Iraq and from rock salt. Salt water creeping into the Sawad's fields is a growing problem. Local: salt flats near Basra.
- **Dyeing with mordants and vat dyes** [`mordant_dyeing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mordant_dyeing.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Dyers use alum mordants with madder, kermes, saffron and henna, and vat indigo from India. Tiraz workshops weave official inscribed textiles for the caliph. Recipes are workshop secrets. Local: tiraz workshops; dyers' market.
- **Chlorine, bleaching powder and disinfection** [`chlorine_bleach`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/chlorine_bleach.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Linen is bleached by sun, ash lye and sour milk. Chlorine needs an acid from salt.
- **Electrolysis and electroplating** [`electrolysis`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/electrolysis.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. No current, no zinc. Bitumen (qir) from Hit on the Euphrates waterproofs boats, roofs and baths; naphtha (naft) from springs in Iraq, Khuzistan and Baku feeds lamps and the army's fire troops. Distilling a light white naphtha is described by al-Razi around 900. Local: bitumen wells of Hit; naffatun (naphtha troops). Elsewhere: Baku, naphtha springs.
